newsitem.title: USA: U.S. could hike beef exports to Hong Kong - attache.
newsitem.headline: U.S. could hike beef exports to Hong Kong - attache.

text.p: U.S. beef exporters are "missing out" on substantial demand in Hong Kong for middle-market beef products, according to a U.S. agricultural attache report made public on Wednesday.
In a report prepared by the U.S. embassy on June 25, the attache said Hong Kong's consumption of beef will grow at a modest rate of about 5 percent annually over the next few years.

"At present, the United States is exporting higher quality up-market beef products into Hong Kong. The United States is missing out on participation in all but a niche sector of the market," the report said. "There is a substantial market for middle-market products -- a market which U.S. exporters are not targeting, but their competitors are."
Most beef imported by Hong Kong comes from Australia, New Zealand and the United States. China also supplies live cattle and frozen beef.
Hong Kong's pork market is dominated by imports of live Chinese pigs, with only a tiny market for fresh or chilled pork, the report said. Frozen pork imports totaled 70,000 tonnes in 1995.

"Because China dominates the import market for pork into Hong Kong, both in live pigs and in fresh and frozen pork, it will be very difficult for U.S. exporters to expand market share here," the attache said. "The U.S. is a small player and at best it should try to maintain the modest position that it already holds."

U.S. exports currently dominate the Hong Kong market for frozen and fresh poultry but products such as chicken feet and offals could face competition from China, Australia and other suppliers, the report said.
In 1995, Hong Kong ranked as the eighth largest recipient territory of U.S. agricultural exports, totaling $1.5 billion.

The report also said that U.S. export companies are targeting safer, high margin, top-end food service sector outlets which has left nearly 95 percent of Hong Kong's restaurant market "untapped" by U.S. exporters. The fastest growing restaurant segment in Hong Kong is non-Chinese restaurants and fast-food restaurants.
